To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the use of a knowledge base editor allows the formalization of the knowledge of regulatory texts, (ii) the formalization of these texts allows the development of a knowledge base that can be used to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and (iii) the knowledge base can be used to develop a tool that can assist the OHS professional in his or her work.

(i) the ontology is a model that formalizes the knowledge of a community of actors; (ii) it is a tool that facilitates communication between the information system and the community of actors and (iii) it can be implemented in the form of a knowledge base.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an ontology and the associated knowledge bases that can be used by OHS professionals for the management of their compliance with regulatory requirements.
the development of a knowledge base for the management of OHS compliance.
the formalization of legal knowledge for the management of regulatory texts and the creation of knowledge base tools to ensure the effective management of compliance in occupational health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methodology and the associated software tool are useful in the formalization of legal compliance knowledge in occupational health and Safety.
the use of ontologies in the design of knowledge bases for regulatory monitoring is a viable approach.
the ontology and knowledge base are a useful and effective way of managing legal compliance in OHS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ontologies and knowledge base systems are powerful tools for formalising regulatory knowledge.
we have developed a methodology for the creation of ontologies and the associated knowledge bases for the purpose of ensuring compliance with the law.
the ontology and knowledge base can be used to create a knowledge base for the management of OHS compliance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of ontologies and rule-based knowledge bases can be used to create a common language between OHS professionals and information systems.
an ontology can be used as a tool for the formalization and structuring of legal texts and that the use of a knowledge base can make it easier to exploit this information in an automated way.
it is possible to formalize the regulatory knowledge of a given domain (OHS) and to create a knowledge base that is accessible and exploitable by a wide range of users.
